quiz_exm2:1.q: What is the classification of this epithelium?
quiz_exm2:1.r: Transitional epithelium of the bladder: several layers, with dome shaped apical cytoplasm in the surface cells and scattered binucleated cells (p. 142). Stratified squamous would have flattened surface cells.
quiz_exm2:1.alt: Light micrograph of a multilayered epithelium resting on connective tissue.

quiz_exm2:10.q: Which substance is stored in the specific granules of this leukocyte?
quiz_exm2:10.r: These are eosinophils (bilobed nucleus, coarse red-orange granules, p. 394). The crystalline internum of their granules holds major basic protein, eosinophil cationic protein and neurotoxin (p. 395). Heparin, histamine and eosinophil chemotactic factor are basophil products (p. 402).
quiz_exm2:10.alt: Two blood smear fields, each with one granulated nucleated cell among red cells.

quiz_exm2:11.q: An epithelium has dome shaped surface cells, some of them binucleated. According to the lecture's location table, which site does this type line?
quiz_exm2:11.r: Transitional epithelium lines the urinary system from the renal calyces to the urethra (p. 143; features on p. 142). Epididymis is pseudostratified, esophagus stratified squamous, gallbladder simple columnar, sweat gland ducts stratified cuboidal.

quiz_exm2:12.q: After the normoblast expels its nucleus, the cell still shows residual RNA staining in its cytoplasm. What is this cell called?
quiz_exm2:12.r: Reticulocyte: no nucleus, with residual RNA staining in the cytoplasm; the erythrocyte has no nucleus and uniform eosinophilic cytoplasm (p. 1154). The nucleus is ejected at the normoblast stage (p. 463).

quiz_exm2:13.q: In this part of the lecture's diagram of collagen synthesis, enzymes acting at the two short arrows remove the end pieces marked by asterisks. What is the product, and where is it formed?
quiz_exm2:13.r: Procollagen is discharged to the extracellular space, where procollagen peptidases cleave the registration peptides, turning it into insoluble tropocollagen, which aggregates into fibrils (p. 954).
quiz_exm2:13.alt: Line diagram of a triple helix with frayed ends marked by asterisks, and below it the same helix with the ends detached.

quiz_exm2:14.q: What is the small appendage at the arrow tip, attached to the nucleus of this cell?
quiz_exm2:14.r: The drumstick on a neutrophil nucleus is the Barr body, the inactive X chromosome of a female patient (p. 386, p. 1147).
quiz_exm2:14.alt: Blood smear with two nucleated cells with lobed nuclei; an arrow points to a small projection on one nucleus.

quiz_exm2:15.q: Goblet cell mucus is rich in glycoproteins, and hepatocytes store glycogen. Which stain on the lecture's list demonstrates both?
quiz_exm2:15.r: Periodic Acid Schiff stains glycogen and glycoproteins (p. 103). Orcein and aldehyde fuchsin are for elastic fibers and silver is for reticular fibers and the Golgi apparatus.

quiz_exm2:16.q: These nuclear outlines from the lecture's diagram run left to right in order of granulocyte maturation. Which stage comes directly after the one at the arrow?
quiz_exm2:16.r: The arrowed outline has a bean shaped nucleus, so it is a metamyelocyte; the next stage is the band cell with a horse shoe shaped nucleus, then the segmented cell (p. 472, p. 470, p. 1155).
quiz_exm2:16.alt: Four schematic cells in a row with black nuclei of different shapes; a yellow arrow marks the second.

quiz_exm2:17.q: What is the classification of this ciliated epithelium?
quiz_exm2:17.r: Pseudostratified epithelium of the trachea: nuclei at several levels, cilia and goblet cells, but one layer of cells (p. 141, p. 143). Transitional epithelium has dome shaped surface cells and no cilia (p. 142).
quiz_exm2:17.alt: Light micrograph of a tall epithelium with nuclei at several levels and a fringed surface.

quiz_exm2:18.q: A patient with a poor diet has the gum and skin findings shown. Per the lecture's table, the missing nutrient is a cofactor for which enzyme?
quiz_exm2:18.r: Scurvy results from lack of vitamin C, the cofactor for proline hydroxylase, giving ulceration of gums and hemorrhages (p. 957, p. 958).
quiz_exm2:18.alt: Four clinical photographs: swollen gums, a spotted rash on skin, fingers, and bruised legs.

quiz_exm2:19.q: A woman has leukocytes 8,000/mm3, hematocrit 33%, hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, platelets 300,000/mm3 and 1% reticulocytes. Which value lies outside the lecture's normal range?
quiz_exm2:19.r: Normal: leukocytes 4,500-11,000/mm3, hematocrit 36-48% for women, hemoglobin 12.1-15.1 g/dL for women, platelets 150,000-450,000/mm3 (p. 364); reticulocytes about 1% of red cells (p. 467).

quiz_exm2:2.q: Identify the nucleated cell in this smear of normal blood.
quiz_exm2:2.r: Basophil: large dark blue-purple granules that partly hide the nucleus (p. 401, p. 1150). Eosinophil granules are orange-red and neutrophil granules are barely visible.
quiz_exm2:2.alt: Blood smear with a single nucleated cell among red cells.

quiz_exm2:20.q: Which blood cell is shown in this transmission electron micrograph?
quiz_exm2:20.r: Eosinophil: in the electron microscope its specific granules show striped crystals, the crystalline internum (p. 1149, p. 395).
quiz_exm2:20.alt: Electron micrograph of one cell with a lobed nucleus and many oval granules that contain dark bars.

quiz_exm2:21.q: Panels a to e show red cell formation in order. Which panel shows the last stage that still has a nucleus, the one that expels it?
quiz_exm2:21.r: Panel d is the orthochromatic erythroblast (normoblast) with a condensed eccentric nucleus (p. 1154); the nucleus is ejected at this stage and the cell becomes a reticulocyte (p. 463).
quiz_exm2:21.alt: Five small micrograph panels lettered a to e, joined by arrows.

quiz_exm2:22.q: What are the banded structures in this transmission electron micrograph of connective tissue?
quiz_exm2:22.r: TEM of collagen fibrils, seen in cross and longitudinal section with their cross banding (p. 956). Order of size: tropocollagen, fibril, fiber, fiber bundle (p. 954).
quiz_exm2:22.alt: Electron micrograph with cross-striated rods cut lengthwise and many round profiles cut across.

quiz_exm2:23.q: How long do elements like the small dark one at the yellow arrow stay in the circulation?
quiz_exm2:23.r: The small dark bodies between the red cells are platelets (p. 420); platelets spend 10 days in circulation (p. 421).
quiz_exm2:23.alt: Blood smear with large red cells and a few small dark bodies; a yellow arrow marks one small body.

quiz_exm2:24.q: Both panels show the same type of leukocyte from blood. Besides taking part in inflammation, what does this cell do according to the lecture?
quiz_exm2:24.r: These are basophils: large granules partly obscure the nucleus (p. 1150). Their functions are inflammation and recruiting eosinophils through eosinophil chemotactic factor (p. 402).
quiz_exm2:24.alt: Two light micrograph panels, each with one cell packed with large dark granules.

quiz_exm2:25.q: A magenta, Periodic Acid Schiff positive line is seen under an epithelium by light microscopy. By the course definition, what is this line?
quiz_exm2:25.r: The course defines the basement membrane as a PAS-positive layer visible at the light microscopic level, while the basal lamina is visible only by TEM (p. 130).

quiz_exm2:26.q: This patient also has frequent joint dislocations. Per the lecture's table of collagen disorders, which defect fits best?
o: Lack of vitamin C in the diet
One nucleotide change in type I genes
quiz_exm2:26.r: Hyperextensible finger joints are shown for Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (p. 959). In the table, increased articular mobility and frequent luxation belong to type VII: decrease in procollagen peptidase activity (p. 957).
quiz_exm2:26.alt: Photograph of a hand with a finger bent far backwards.

quiz_exm2:27.q: What share of the leukocytes in normal blood does the type of nucleated cell shown here make up?
quiz_exm2:27.r: The cell is an eosinophil: bilobed nucleus and coarse red granules (p. 428, p. 394). Eosinophils are 2-4% of leukocytes, fourth in the order neutrophil, lymphocyte, monocyte, eosinophil, basophil (p. 364).
quiz_exm2:27.alt: Blood smear with a single granulated nucleated cell among red cells.

quiz_exm2:28.q: According to the lecture, what does an accumulation of cells like the one at the blue arrow in the blood indicate?
quiz_exm2:28.r: The arrowed cell is a band (immature) neutrophil with a horse shoe shaped nucleus (p. 427, p. 365). Band neutrophil accumulation in blood indicates bacterial infection (p. 474).
quiz_exm2:28.alt: Blood smear with two nucleated cells among red cells; a blue arrow points up at one of them.

quiz_exm2:29.q: Which features of the arrowed surface cell, noted on the slide, set this epithelium apart from stratified squamous epithelium?
o: Ciliated with a basal body row
Columnar with a striated brush border
quiz_exm2:29.r: Transitional epithelium (bladder) has dome shaped apical cytoplasm and scattered binucleated cells in its surface layer (p. 142); stratified squamous has flattened surface cells.
quiz_exm2:29.alt: Close view of the surface layer of an epithelium; a black arrow points into one large surface cell.

quiz_exm2:3.q: In the rough endoplasmic reticulum, specific residues of the new collagen alpha chains are hydroxylated in a vitamin dependent step. Which residues and which vitamin?
quiz_exm2:3.r: The synthesis diagram states: hydroxylation of specific prolyl and lysyl residues in the endoplasmic reticulum, vitamin C dependent (p. 954). The table adds that vitamin C is the cofactor for proline hydroxylase (p. 957).

quiz_exm2:30.q: Cells like the one at the yellow arrow, shown with cresyl blue, make up 8% of a patient's red cells. Per the lecture's key point, what may this indicate?
quiz_exm2:30.r: Supravital cresyl blue shows the residual RNA of reticulocytes. Normally about 1% of red cells in blood are reticulocytes; excess reticulocytes may indicate anemia (p. 467).
quiz_exm2:30.alt: Smear of anucleate cells, some containing dark blue clumps; a yellow arrow marks one with clumps.

quiz_exm2:31.q: Which sequence lists the forms of collagen in the order in which they arise?
quiz_exm2:31.r: Procollagen (triple helix with registration peptides) is secreted, cleaved to tropocollagen, which aggregates into fibrils; fibrils form fibers and fiber bundles (p. 954).

quiz_exm2:32.q: What do the azurophilic granules of the cells with lobed nuclei shown here contain?
quiz_exm2:32.r: These are neutrophils with multilobulated nuclei (p. 1147). Their azurophilic (non-specific, primary lysosome) granules hold myeloperoxidase and acid hydrolases; the specific granules hold proteases and lysozyme (p. 387).
quiz_exm2:32.alt: Blood smear with three nucleated cells with multilobed nuclei among red cells.

quiz_exm2:4.q: What is the cell at the arrow in this row of marrow cells?
quiz_exm2:4.r: The orthochromatic erythroblast (normoblast) is the smallest nucleated red cell precursor, with a small condensed nucleus and pink cytoplasm (p. 1153, p. 1154). It is the last stage with a nucleus.
quiz_exm2:4.alt: Row of four nucleated marrow cells of decreasing size; the last one is marked by an arrow.

quiz_exm2:5.q: In normal blood, where does the leukocyte at the yellow arrow rank in frequency among the leukocytes?
quiz_exm2:5.r: The arrowed cell is a lymphocyte: round dark nucleus filling most of the cell (p. 365). Order is Never Let Monkeys Eat Bananas: neutrophil 60-70%, lymphocyte 28%, monocyte 5%, eosinophil 2-4%, basophil 0.5% (p. 364).
quiz_exm2:5.alt: Blood smear with several nucleated cells among red cells; one is marked by a yellow arrow.

quiz_exm2:6.q: Which stain does the lecture name as the most common one for visualizing fibers like the thin dark one at the arrow tip?
quiz_exm2:6.r: The thin dark branching fibers are elastic fibers; orcein is the most common stain (brownish-red) to visualize elastic fibers in tissue sections (p. 963, p. 103). Silver is for reticular fibers.
quiz_exm2:6.alt: Spread of connective tissue with thick pink bands and thin dark fibers; an arrow marks one thin fiber.

quiz_exm2:7.q: Identify the nucleated cell in this marrow smear.
quiz_exm2:7.r: Band cell: horse shoe shaped nucleus without segmentation (p. 1174, p. 1159). A metamyelocyte nucleus is only bean shaped and a mature granulocyte nucleus is segmented (p. 1155).
quiz_exm2:7.alt: Smear with one nucleated cell among red cells.

quiz_exm2:8.q: What is the thick pink band at the arrow tip in this light micrograph of mesentery?
quiz_exm2:8.r: The thick pink bands in the mesentery spread are collagen fibers; the thin dark ones are elastic fibers (p. 955). Fibrils and tropocollagen are below light microscope resolution (p. 954, p. 956).
quiz_exm2:8.alt: Spread of connective tissue with thick pink bands and thin dark fibers; an arrow marks a thick band.

quiz_exm2:9.q: What are the small purple bodies at the yellow arrow in this normal blood smear?
quiz_exm2:9.r: Platelets are much smaller than all other cellular components of blood (p. 1145) and often lie in small clumps (p. 429).
quiz_exm2:9.alt: Blood smear with red cells and scattered small purple bodies; a yellow arrow marks a cluster of them.

brief:
Tip Sheet: Identify and Explain (Examinus)

These are the topics classmates passed on from the lecturer. Every fact is from the slides; page numbers are pages of the combined PDF.

1. Urothelium (transitional epithelium)

Feature Fact Page
Surface cells Dome shaped, sometimes binucleated 142
Where Urinary system, renal calyces to urethra 143
Not stratified squamous Stratified squamous has flattened surface cells 142
Not pseudostratified Pseudostratified, as in the trachea, has cilia and goblet cells and is one layer 141

2. Two stains

Stain Shows Page
Orcein Elastic fibers; the most common elastic stain 103, 963
Periodic Acid Schiff Glycogen and glycoproteins; the basement membrane 103, 130

3. Collagen synthesis in order

Step Where Page
Alpha chains made with registration peptides; signal peptide clipped Rough endoplasmic reticulum 954
Hydroxylation of proline and lysine; vitamin C dependent Endoplasmic reticulum 954
Sugars added to hydroxylysine Endoplasmic reticulum 954
Triple helix forms: procollagen Endoplasmic reticulum 954
Packaging and secretion Golgi, secretory vesicles 954
Procollagen peptidases clip the registration peptides: tropocollagen Outside the cell 954
Tropocollagen aggregates into fibrils; lysyl oxidase cross-links them Outside the cell 954

Size order: tropocollagen, fibril, fiber, fiber bundle (p. 954).

Disorder Defect Signs Page
Scurvy No vitamin C, the cofactor for proline hydroxylase Gum ulcers, hemorrhages 957
Ehlers-Danlos type IV Faulty type III transcription or translation Aortic or intestinal rupture 957
Ehlers-Danlos type VI Faulty lysine hydroxylation Stretchy skin, eyeball rupture 957
Ehlers-Danlos type VII Low procollagen peptidase activity Loose joints, frequent dislocation 957
Osteogenesis imperfecta One nucleotide change in type I genes Spontaneous fractures 957

4. Red cell line

Stage Time Note Page
Proerythroblast 20 hours 463
Basophilic erythroblast 20 hours 463
Polychromatophilic erythroblast 25 hours 463
Orthochromatophilic erythroblast (normoblast) 30 hours Last stage with a nucleus; the nucleus is ejected here 463
Reticulocyte 3 days No nucleus, residual RNA; about 1% of red cells; more may mean anemia 463, 467
Erythrocyte 463

5. Telling the granulocytes apart

Cell On a smear Key fact Page
Neutrophil Multilobed nucleus, faint granules; drumstick is the inactive X chromosome Azurophilic granules: myeloperoxidase, acid hydrolases. Specific granules: proteases, lysozyme 386–387
Eosinophil Bilobed nucleus, coarse red-orange granules Major basic protein in the crystalline internum; attacks parasites 394–395
Basophil Dark granules that hide the nucleus Heparin, histamine, eosinophil chemotactic factor; inflammation, recruits eosinophils 401–402
Band cell Horseshoe nucleus, not yet segmented Many in blood means bacterial infection. Comes after the metamyelocyte (bean nucleus) 472, 474

6. Normal numbers

Leukocyte Share Job Page
Neutrophil 60–70% Attack bacteria 364
Lymphocyte 28% Humoral and cellular immunity 364
Monocyte 5% Become phagocytic macrophages 364
Eosinophil 2–4% Attack parasites 364
Basophil 0.5% Mediate inflammation 364

Never let monkeys eat bananas.

Value Normal Page
Leukocytes 4,500–11,000 per cubic millimetre 364
Platelets 150,000–450,000 per cubic millimetre 364
Hematocrit Women 36–48%, men 40–54% 364
Hemoglobin Women 12.1–15.1, men 13.8–17.2 grams per decilitre 364

7. Platelets

Feature Fact Page
On a smear Small purple bodies, much smaller than any cell, often in clumps 429, 1145
Lifespan 10 days in circulation 421
